My family has worked this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 10 mu. The soil is decent loam — good for wheat and corn. That is what I grow. That is what everyone around here grows. Wheat goes in the ground in October and I harvest it in June, then I plant corn right after on the same land. Two crops, one year, same plot.

I buy my wheat seed from the village supply cooperative — they sell Jimai 22, which my neighbor has used for years and gets a reliable yield. For corn I use Xianyu 335, a hybrid. The seed shop pushes it and my cousin used it last year and got a decent harvest. I will use that.

For fertilizer, I put down a good amount before planting wheat — diammonium phosphate and urea. I top-dress again at jointing. I am not stingy with nitrogen because one bad year can hurt the whole family. For corn I put down base fertilizer at planting and chase it once during the big growth push. Water is a concern — the well is getting deeper every year — but wheat needs to be irrigated or the yield collapses. I irrigate three times for wheat: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. For corn the summer rain usually helps so I only pump twice unless it is a dry year.

I rotary till after the corn harvest to prepare for wheat. For corn I seed directly into the wheat stubble — saves time and the machine can do it.
